subject: NorthGrid renewal — capacity uplift & pricing options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Cho <emma.cho@northgrid.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: NorthGrid renewal — capacity uplift & pricing options

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for taking time last week — great to see how quickly your team is ramping up production traffic. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a few concrete options on the table to make the renewal simpler and protect you on price while giving you room to scale over the next 12 months.

High-level context: current committed level = 1.5M tokens/month; you expect ~1.8-2.0x growth if the new recommendation engine is fully rolled out. You mentioned wanting predictable unit economics for the next 6–12 months and the ability to absorb a burst in Q3.

Options we can offer (intend to be pragmatic — pick one + a fallback):
- Option A — 12mo committed uplift: 40% increase to committed tokens, 10% list discount on committed units, quarterly true-up (standard).
- Option B — Short-term price-hold + burst credits: 6-month price-hold at current effective rate, includes a 200k-token burst credit pool for unexpected peaks. After 6 months, convert to either pay-as-you-go or a revised commit.
- Option C — Milestone credits + flexible commit: 6-month trial of increased capacity where we provide usage credits tied to onboarding milestones (e.g., integration completion, 1st production traffic, 90-day SLA baseline).

Operational notes: we can do per-route quotas so the recommendation traffic is prioritized and stays within your SLOs. If procurement needs a single line-item illustration, I attached a simple forecast template (NG-usage-forecast-template.xlsx) with the uplift scenarios and estimated monthly spend under each option.

Would you be open to Option B (price-hold then convert) as a starting point? If procurement needs to see legal-friendly language, I can circulate a short term-sheet.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the expected uplift range (conservative / expected / stretch) in the attached sheet.
2) If you like Option B, we draft a 1-page amendment that covers the 6-month price-hold + burst credits and route to procurement/legal.
3) Internal sync on our side for final T&Cs (I’ll loop David and Monica).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0137
Redwood Inference

Attachment: NG-usage-forecast-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Emma Cho <emma.cho@northgrid.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NorthGrid renewal — capacity uplift & pricing options

Vanessa — thanks for the clear options and the template.

Quick answers: our procurement timeline is tight — we need a signed amendment by the end of March to align with our budget cycle. Forecast (conservative/expected/stretch) is attached in the template — expected is ~1.9x current spend in the next 6 months as the recommender rolls out.

A few asks from our side:
- Price-hold is attractive, but procurement requires either a 6-month hold + guaranteed step-up pricing for months 7–12, or an automatic review with a max step-up of 8% (to avoid large unexpected increases).
- We need the burst credits to apply across model variants (not just the primary route) because we may shift traffic between gpt-style models during testing.
- Legal will want a short amendment or addendum; could you provide a simple 1-page term sheet we can share with them?

I’m CCing procurement@northgrid.ai — they’ll push the DocuSign once we agree language. We don’t need a full SOW, just the amendment and a short invoice example so finance knows how credits show up.

Emma Cho
Head of Platform, NorthGrid Technologies
emma.cho@northgrid.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: NorthGrid renewal — capacity uplift & pricing options

David / Monica — forwarding Emma's reply. Procurement wants a signed amendment by EOM; they like the price-hold idea but want either a capped step-up (8%) or a guaranteed step-up schedule. They also need burst credits to be model-agnostic and a one-page term sheet for legal.

My recommendation (to keep the deal moving and limit exposure):
- Offer: 6-month price-hold at current effective rate + 250k-token burst credit pool usable across routes.
- Guarantee: months 7–12 can come up to a maximum 8% increase vs the held rate OR the customer can elect to convert to a 12-month committed uplift at the earlier proposed discount (10% on committed units).
- Billing/true-up: quarterly true-ups with a one-line credit application on month-end invoices to consume burst credits; we show examples in the attached draft term-sheet.

Rationale: keeps procurement comfortable (short firm commitment), gives NorthGrid immediate predictability, and preserves our ability to convert to a higher-commit deal if they prefer stability. It matches the spirit of Option B while being slightly more generous on burst credits to close quickly.

If you’re good with the economics I’ll send the attached term-sheet to Emma and CC legal for redlines. If not, please propose edits.

Best,
Vanessa

Attachment: NorthGrid-term-sheet-draft-v1.pdf (term sheet, 1 page)

From: Emma Cho <emma.cho@northgrid.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@northgrid.ai
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NorthGrid renewal — capacity uplift & pricing options

Vanessa — this looks reasonable and procurement has reviewed the 1-pager. They asked for two small clarifications (both minor):
1) Spell out that burst credits are shared across model variants and are consumed before invoice-level overages.
2) Add an explicit line that any unused burst credits expire at the end of the 6-month hold period (not transferable).

Procurement has routed the 1-pager to Legal for a quick redline; I’ll drop the DocuSign request once the redline is in. You can expect our legal to return comments by end of day Wednesday.

If you can send an invoice example that shows how the credits would appear (line item + applied credit row) that would help finance sign off quickly.

Thanks for moving fast on this — we’d like to get the amendment signed and in effect by 31 Mar.

Emma
